text:
marta (security): heads up — we just got an EU DSAR asking for full deletion for user id 7f9b. They claim data was exported to a partner workspace in jan. Need immediate coord: RBAC lock, audit export, partner deletion confirmation, and KMS snapshot check :eyes:
kevin (infra): ack. can you paste the partner export details? we need the s3 path + access key used by the export job
marta (security): partner S3: s3://partner-prod-exports/redwood/dumps/2025-01-12/embeddings-7f9b.ndjson. Exported by service-account `sa-emb-exporter@prod`. KMS key: projects/redwood/keys/emb-exports-key (customer-managed).
li (eng-sre): putting `sa-emb-exporter` into a deny policy now (will block new reads). ETA ~3m. :lock:
infra-bot: policy-update: `sa-emb-exporter` role removed from prod-export-bucket — request id u-9c3f.
sam (product): do we need a retention exception to stop normal tombstone/purge runs while we coordinate?
kevin (infra): yes — if the normal TTL job runs, the object might be tombstoned before partner confirms deletion. open retention-exception ticket with retention-team and mark as DSAR-critical. I'll pause any scheduled key rotations for `emb-exports-key`.
marta (security): opening retention exception now. tagging legal. olivia — can you confirm if partner deletion acceptance is enough or we need a signed attestation? :thinking:
olivia (legal): for EU DSAR erasure, we prefer partner-signed deletion certificate and a SHA256 checksum of the deleted object + timestamp. If partner refuses/doesn't respond in 7 days, escalate to contractual remedy. I'll draft notice.
li (eng-sre): grabbed recent access logs for that S3 path. snippet: `GET /embeddings-7f9b.ndjson 200` from IP 34.82.10.4 on 2025-01-12 by `sa-emb-exporter`. I'll attach full log to the retention-exception ticket.
marta (security): also discovered during a vuln triage: the logshipper (v2.3.1) had an out-of-window token leak that could have briefly exposed object keys to our internal dev logs earlier this year. No evidence yet partner pulled them, but we must treat as potential. :warning:
kevin (infra): timeline? which deploy has v2.3.1? we should rotate any long-lived credentials referenced in those logs and revoke old access keys immediately.
li (eng-sre): v2.3.1 was deployed on 2025-02-03 in `logging-fleet`. I'll isolate the cluster and start an integrity snapshot.
sam (product): product asks — do we return 'erased' to user now or wait for partner attestation + evidence we scrubbed logs?
olivia (legal): wait for partner attestation OR documented proof we removed all copies we control. If we have to rely on partner, we need their signed attestation. Also loop in DPO if this escalates.
marta (security): action list: 1) kevin pause rotations + block SA (in progress) 2) li export full audit trail to secure evidence bucket (encrypted) 3) sam manage DSAR comms and set user expectation to 30 days 4) olivia request partner attestation + start contractual escalation if no reply in 7 days 5) me — coordinate vuln triage and notify DPO.
kevin (infra): done on pause rotations for `emb-exports-key` and disabled `sa-emb-exporter` (see infra-bot request id u-9c3f). Not rotating until we get confirmation from legal.
infra-bot: key-rotation: scheduled job for `emb-exports-key` cancelled for 7 days by kevin.
li (eng-sre): uploaded logs to `s3://redwood-evidence/dsar/3012345678/` encrypted with keystore `evidence-kms`. sharing link to retention ticket.
marta (security): thanks. sam — please update the user message to say: "we've initiated deletion and are coordinating deletion verification with third-party partner; you will receive confirmation within 30 days." keep it conservative.
sam (product): will do. drafting now. ping me if legal wants different wording.
olivia (legal): starting partner attestation request email now. cc: DPO. I'll also request chain-of-custody details for the exported file (checksums, access logs, deletion proof).
marta (security): quick technical Q for eng-sre: if partner provides a deletion statement but still we have an encrypted snapshot under `emb-exports-key` in our archival storage, do we need to destroy KMS material as well?
li (eng-sre): if the snapshot is still encrypted with `emb-exports-key` and it's within our control, we must delete the object and then schedule KMS key rotation/destruction per legal guidance. But do NOT destroy the key until legal confirms it's safe — forensic hold might require access.
kevin (infra): agree. we'll hold key material; if legal signs off we can schedule `key-destruction` workflow.
marta (security): noted. I'll update incident tracker and label as `dsar+possible-exposure`. If partner doesn't confirm, we escalate to contracts and DPO.
olivia (legal): uploaded draft notice to contracts channel. tagging contracts lead.
kevin (infra): one more technical: we should run a check for any other exported files with the same user id pattern, running query: ```sql
SELECT path FROM exports WHERE contains(path, '7f9b') OR metadata ->> 'user_id' = '7f9b';
```
li (eng-sre): running that now. will post results. :mag:
marta (security): thanks everyone. please add any further evidences to the retention-exception ticket. I'll coordinate follow-ups here. :thumbsup:
